## My thinking this year

I've been farming this land more than fifty years, so I don't overthink it. I know what works here. This year I'll do like always — put about 12 mu in cotton and keep the other 8 mu in wheat-maize double crop. The cotton is where most of my cash comes from, but wheat gives us the flour for the family, and the maize after wheat helps feed the pigs and gives a little extra to sell.

My wife and I do most of the work. My son works in town and only helps on weekends when it's busy — picking cotton, or pulling wheat off the ground in June. For cotton picking I'll need to hire a few people from the village, my back can't take all that bending anymore. For the wheat-maize I can mostly manage with family.

**Cotton (12 mu).** I'll plant around April 20, same as every year. I buy seed from the town shop — the usual variety, nothing fancy, about 40 yuan per mu for seed. Before planting I spread about one bag of compound fertilizer (that's 15-15-15, 40 kg) per mu, so roughly 6 kg of nitrogen from that. Then when the cotton is flowering I'll topdress urea, maybe 15 kg per mu. I'll irrigate once before planting if the soil is dry, and once or twice in July-August if there's no rain. Cotton uses water but pumping costs money so I don't overdo it. I'll spray for bollworm when I see them, probably 3-4 times over the summer. Last year I got about 240 kg of lint per mu, this year I expect similar if the weather holds.

**Wheat (8 mu).** Already planted last October. Base fertilizer went down then — one bag of diammonium phosphate per mu. In March when the wheat starts jointing I'll topdress urea, about 15 kg per mu. If the wheat looks yellow I might add a little more. I'll irrigate 3 times — once in spring for green-up, once at jointing, once at grain-filling. That's the normal way here. I usually get around 420 kg per mu. Harvest mid-June.

**Maize (8 mu).** Right after wheat harvest, same field. Only about 5 days to get the maize in the ground — we work fast. I don't plow, I just use the no-till planter that the neighbor has (I pay him by the mu). Base fertilizer goes with the planter, about 20 kg of compound per mu. Then at the big bell stage I topdress 15 kg urea. Usually one irrigation in late July if it's dry. I spray for armyworm if I see damage. Yield around 480 kg per mu normally.

I'm not going to try anything new this year. Fertilizer prices are up a little but cotton price looked okay last fall so I'm keeping things the same.
